title: The Smart Monkey
source_note: NCERT structural and thematic alignment only. All teaching passages, checks, feedback, and assessment situations are original Zidd content.

levels.title: Follow the clean-up sequence
levels.focus: track what is used, dropped, noticed, and put away
levels.teaching_goal: Read an original market-break scene and connect each object with the action that changes the place.

guided_check.teaching_block: Follow the object through the scene. Bought tells what came first; dropped tells what made the mess.
guided_check.passage: Nadia buys roasted corn at a market stall. After eating, she drops the paper sleeve beside a bench.

bridge.teaching_block: Now track who notices the litter. Do not choose the person who dropped it unless the sentence says so.
bridge.passage: A monkey on the wall sees the sleeve. It carries its own fruit peel toward a green bin.
bridge.prompt: Who carries a peel toward the bin?

masterclass.teaching_block: Keep the final action separate from the lesson. First identify what the person physically does.
masterclass.passage: Nadia watches the monkey use the bin. She picks up her sleeve and places it inside too.
masterclass.prompt: What does Nadia put in the bin?

independent_check.teaching_block: Read a new clean-up chain without choices. Match each object to its owner and final place.
independent_check.passage: After lunch, Zubin folds his foil. Lata gathers two orange peels. Both walk to the waste basket.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer sequence tracking to a bus stop. Notice which action happens after the wind moves the paper.
transfer_check.passage: A ticket slips from a pocket and blows under a seat. The passenger reaches down, picks it up, and uses the bin.
transfer_check.prompt: What happens after the ticket blows under the seat?
accepted_answers: the passenger reaches down and picks it up

levels.title: Learn from a smart example
levels.focus: infer how one responsible action changes another person's choice
levels.teaching_goal: Connect the monkey's example with the observers' changed behaviour and the larger cleanliness message.

guided_check.teaching_block: An example teaches through action. The observer changes only after seeing the responsible choice.
guided_check.passage: Two children leave cups on a step. A monkey carries its peel to the bin. The children look at one another and return for their cups.
options: The monkey's action reminds them to clean up.
accepted_answers: The monkey's action reminds them to clean up.
because they see the monkey use the bin

bridge.teaching_block: Choose the main idea that covers both the example and the change. Avoid an answer about monkeys being better than people.
bridge.passage: A vendor sorts waste into two bins. Nearby shoppers begin placing fruit scraps and paper in the matching bins.
options: A good example can guide others.
accepted_answers: A good example can guide others.
people can learn from a good example

masterclass.teaching_block: Smart here means making a sensible choice. It is not about tricks or getting a prize.
masterclass.passage: The monkey keeps the path safe by putting a slippery peel in the bin.
masterclass.prompt: Why is this a smart action?
accepted_answers: because it keeps the path safe
because someone could slip on the peel

independent_check.teaching_block: Explain the change in your own words. Include what is seen and what the observer does next.
independent_check.passage: Rakesh is about to leave a juice box on a wall. He sees a younger child carry paper to a bin, so he turns back and disposes of the box properly.
independent_check.prompt: How does the younger child influence Rakesh?

concept_slots.description: Mention the child using the bin.
Mention Rakesh changing his action.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer learning-by-example to saving water. State the model action and the copied action.
transfer_check.passage: At a wash area, Ena closes the tap while soaping her hands. Her cousin notices and closes his tap too.
transfer_check.prompt: What lesson does the cousin learn from Ena?

concept_slots.description: Identify Ena's water-saving action.
Show that the cousin follows the example.

levels.title: Understand clean-place words
levels.focus: use context to understand litter, empty, nearby, and ashamed
levels.teaching_goal: Infer chapter words from visible actions and results rather than memorising isolated definitions.

guided_check.teaching_block: Litter is waste left in the wrong place. The clue is that wrappers and cups are scattered on the ground.
guided_check.passage: After the fair, litter covers the grass: torn tickets, cups, and food wrappers lie everywhere.
accepted_answers: trash left in the wrong place

bridge.teaching_block: Empty means nothing is left inside. Do not choose open; a box can be open and still contain things.
bridge.passage: Mira tips the packet, but no nuts fall out. The packet is empty.

masterclass.teaching_block: Nearby means not far away. Use the short walking distance as the clue.
masterclass.passage: The bin is nearby, only three steps from the bench.

independent_check.teaching_block: Ashamed describes regret after knowing an action was wrong. It is different from being frightened by danger.
independent_check.passage: Punit sees a cleaner pick up the wrapper he dropped. He feels ashamed and apologises.
accepted_answers: feeling sorry for a wrong action

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use context in a new sports setting. The clue is that every drop has been drunk.
transfer_check.passage: After practice, the water cooler is empty; not one cup can be filled.

levels.title: Choose precise clean-up actions
levels.focus: use pick up, sort, wipe, and dispose in suitable situations
levels.teaching_goal: Match each cleanliness action with the object and result it describes.

guided_check.teaching_block: Pick up means lift something from a surface. It comes before carrying or throwing it away.
guided_check.passage: A wrapper lies by the gate. Please ____ it before the wind blows it away.

bridge.teaching_block: Sort means put different kinds into groups. Look for two bins or two categories.
bridge.passage: We ____ paper and fruit scraps into separate bins.

masterclass.teaching_block: Wipe is used for a wet or dirty surface. It does not mean sweep dry leaves with a broom.
masterclass.passage: Juice spills on the table, so Aman uses a cloth to ____ it.

independent_check.teaching_block: Dispose of means put waste in the correct place. The object is no longer needed.
independent_check.passage: The snack packet is empty. We should ____ it in the marked bin.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Apply two clean-up actions at a picnic. Include handling the mess and using the right waste place.
transfer_check.passage: After a picnic, crumbs remain on the mat and paper plates are beside it.
transfer_check.prompt: Write a short clean-up instruction using two suitable actions.

concept_slots.description: Include cleaning the mat.
Include collecting and binning the plates.

levels.title: Join actions with reasons
levels.focus: use because and but to explain clean choices and contrasts
levels.teaching_goal: Choose because for a reason and but for a contrast in cleanliness sentences.

guided_check.teaching_block: Because answers why. The second idea gives the safety reason for the first action.
guided_check.passage: We put the peel in the bin ____ someone could slip on it.

bridge.teaching_block: But joins two ideas that differ. One person leaves a mess; the other removes it.
bridge.passage: A wrapper fell near the bench, ____ Sohan picked it up.
bridge.prompt: Choose the connector that shows contrast.

masterclass.teaching_block: Decide whether the blank introduces a reason or a different result. Here it explains why the bin is useful.
masterclass.passage: The path stays clear ____ everyone uses the bin.

independent_check.teaching_block: Do not use because when the second idea surprises or contrasts with the first.
independent_check.passage: The bin was close, ____ the visitor left the cup on the wall.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer the connectors to caring for books. Write one reason sentence and one contrast sentence.
transfer_check.passage: The library has a return box. Most children use it, while one book is left on the floor.
transfer_check.prompt: Write two short sentences: one with because and one with but.

concept_slots.description: Use because to explain a careful action.
Use but to contrast the book on the floor.
Refer to the return box or floor book.

levels.title: Explain a responsible choice
levels.focus: write a short reason or friendly reminder about keeping a place clean
levels.teaching_goal: Write respectful, useful messages that name an action and its benefit without blaming a person.

guided_check.teaching_block: A friendly reminder says what to do and gives a helpful reason. It does not call anyone dirty or careless.
guided_check.passage: The class snack area has a bin beside the door.
guided_check.prompt: Which reminder is respectful and useful?
options: Please put wrappers in the bin so our room stays clean.
accepted_answers: Please put wrappers in the bin so our room stays clean.
please put wrappers in the bin so our room stays clean

bridge.teaching_block: A reason answer links the action to a result. Choose the result that is supported by the scene.
bridge.passage: Mehul moves a glass bottle away from the playground and into a recycling bin.
options: It keeps the play area safer.
accepted_answers: It keeps the play area safer.
it keeps the play area safer
because it keeps the playground safe

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass check: use a calm request plus the exact action needed.
masterclass.passage: A friend is about to leave a banana peel under the table.
masterclass.prompt: What short reminder could you give?
accepted_answers: Please put the peel in the bin.
please put the peel in the bin
Put the peel in the bin, please.
put the peel in the bin please

independent_check.teaching_block: Write a flexible reason answer. Include the action and one safety or cleanliness benefit.
independent_check.passage: Sumi collects sharp can lids from a picnic spot and gives them to an adult for safe disposal.

concept_slots.description: Mention collecting or safely disposing of the lids.
Mention safety or cleanliness.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Write a friendly reminder for a new setting. Include a polite action and the benefit to everyone.
transfer_check.passage: At a community garden, empty seed packets are blowing near the plants. A waste basket stands by the gate.
transfer_check.prompt: Write a sign for garden visitors.

concept_slots.description: Ask visitors to use the basket or collect packets.
State a benefit for the garden.

items.passage: Gita unwraps a sandwich, folds the paper, and puts it in her bag until she finds a bin.
items.prompt: Where does Gita keep the paper first?

items.passage: A boy drops a cup. His aunt picks it up and places it in the blue bin.
The cleaner gathers leaves before sweeping the path. She then carries the pile to a compost pit.
items.prompt: Where does the leaf pile go?

items.passage: Arif rinses a reusable cup, dries it, and returns it to the shelf.
items.prompt: What does Arif do after drying the cup?
accepted_answers: he returns it to the shelf

items.passage: One student places scrap paper in a reuse tray. Others begin adding their unused sheets there too.
items.prompt: Which statement best sums up the group's change?
options: A responsible example can guide a group.
accepted_answers: A responsible example can guide a group.
others learn from a responsible example

items.passage: A dog walker ties the waste bag and uses a public bin. Another walker sees this and does the same.
items.prompt: Why does the second walker use the bin?
options: The first walker sets an example.
accepted_answers: The first walker sets an example.
the first walker shows what to do
they learn from the first walker

items.passage: An older child turns off the classroom fan before everyone leaves. Mira notices and checks the lights too.
items.prompt: How does the older child's example affect Mira?

concept_slots.description: Mention switching off the fan.
Mention Mira checking the lights.

items.passage: A fruit seller keeps a basket for peels. Customers begin using it instead of dropping scraps.
items.prompt: Explain the lesson shown by the scene.

concept_slots.description: Mention the basket or seller's example.
Show customers changing to cleaner behaviour.

items.passage: The jar is empty; every biscuit has been eaten.
The broom is nearby, just beside the door.
Litter collects along the fence: straws, paper bits, and wrappers.
After pushing into the queue, Sameer feels ashamed and says sorry.
items.prompt: What does ashamed mean in this sentence?
accepted_answers: feeling sorry about a wrong action

items.passage: Please ____ the paper pieces before they scatter.
We ____ glass and paper into different boxes.
Mud is on the chair. Use a damp cloth to ____ it.
The carton is no longer useful. Please ____ it in the recycling box.
We sweep the steps ____ wet leaves can be slippery.
items.prompt: Choose the connector that introduces the reason.

items.passage: The basket was empty, ____ paper still lay on the floor.
The room smells fresh ____ the windows are open.
Ravi saw the wrapper, ____ he did not walk past it.
A broken cup is beside the play area. Nisha tells an adult and keeps others away.
items.prompt: Which answer explains why Nisha acts responsibly?
options: She protects others from the sharp pieces.
accepted_answers: She protects others from the sharp pieces.
she protects others from the sharp pieces

items.passage: A recycling box stands near the printer.
options: Please place used paper here so it can be recycled.
accepted_answers: Please place used paper here so it can be recycled.
please place used paper here so it can be recycled

items.passage: At the beach, Varun gathers plastic rings and puts them in a covered bin.

concept_slots.description: Mention collecting or binning plastic rings.
Mention protecting the beach or animals.

items.passage: Visitors leave paper cups near a museum bench. A bin is beside the exit.
items.prompt: Write a friendly reminder for visitors.

concept_slots.description: Use a polite clean-up request.
Mention keeping the museum clean or safe.
